components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: How water moves between the oceans, the sky, and the land, again and again.

components.title: Evaporation & Transpiration
components.body:
The sun heats water in oceans, lakes and rivers, turning it from liquid into invisible water vapour that rises into the air. This is **evaporation**.

Plants also release water vapour through tiny pores in their leaves. This is **transpiration**. Together, the two processes are often called *evapotranspiration*.
components.takeaway: Heat energy lifts water into the atmosphere as vapour.

components.title: Condensation
components.body:
As water vapour rises, it cools. Cooler air cannot hold as much vapour, so the vapour condenses into tiny liquid droplets around specks of dust. Billions of these droplets form **clouds**.

The same process makes dew on grass and fog on a cold window.
components.takeaway: Cooling turns vapour back into liquid droplets, which form clouds.

components.title: Precipitation & Collection
components.body:
When cloud droplets join together and grow too heavy to stay in the air, they fall as **precipitation**: rain, snow, sleet or hail.

The water then **collects** in oceans, lakes, rivers, ice caps and underground aquifers. Some runs off the land's surface and some soaks into the ground. From there, the cycle begins again.
components.takeaway: Water returns to Earth and gathers, ready to evaporate once more.

components.title: Following one raindrop
components.body: Imagine a droplet of water in the Pacific Ocean on a hot afternoon. Here is how it moves through the whole cycle.
components.code:
1. Ocean surface warms   → droplet EVAPORATES into vapour
2. Vapour rises ~2 km    → air cools, vapour CONDENSES into a cloud
3. Cloud drifts inland   → droplets merge, fall as rain (PRECIPITATION)
4. Rain lands on a hill  → runs into a river (COLLECTION / runoff)
5. River reaches the sea → back where it started, the cycle repeats
components.code_caption: One complete loop can take days. Water stored in deep groundwater or glaciers may wait thousands of years.
components.takeaway: Every stage is driven by the sun's heat and by gravity.

questions.question: What process turns liquid water into water vapour?
questions.explanation: Evaporation happens when the sun's heat changes liquid water into vapour.

questions.question: Why do clouds form as water vapour rises?
options: The vapour warms up and expands
The vapour cools and condenses into droplets
Plants release droplets into the sky
questions.explanation: Rising air cools. The cooler vapour condenses into tiny droplets that make up clouds.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a form of precipitation?
questions.explanation: Dew forms by condensation directly on surfaces. It does not fall from clouds.
